title: Acts 13:13–41
context: Paul’s company sails to Perga, where John Mark leaves them, and goes on to Pisidian Antioch. Invited to speak in the synagogue, Paul recounts God’s choosing of Israel, the exodus, the judges, and the kings up to David, from whose offspring God has brought Israel a Savior, Jesus. Though Jerusalem’s rulers condemned him, fulfilling the prophets, God raised him from the dead, as the psalms foretold. Through him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed, and everyone who believes is justified from everything the law of Moses could not justify. Paul ends by warning his hearers not to be the scoffers the prophets described.

verses.text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: John Mark leaves them at Perga and returns to Jerusalem. Arminian readers see a failure that later causes conflict but is not final.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God later restoring Mark to usefulness (2 Timothy 4:11).

verses.text: But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.
verses.arminianNotes: They go to the synagogue in Pisidian Antioch on the Sabbath. Arminian commentators see Paul using existing gatherings.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the gospel brought first to Israel.

verses.text: After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”
verses.arminianNotes: The synagogue rulers invite them to speak. Arminian readers see an open door.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see providence providing an opportunity.

verses.text: Paul stood up, and gesturing with his hand said, “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul addresses Israelites and God-fearers. Arminian expositors see the message aimed at both groups.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the gospel addressed to Jews and Gentiles.

verses.text: The God of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they stayed as aliens in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm, he led them out of it.
verses.arminianNotes: God chose the fathers and exalted the people in Egypt. Arminian readers see corporate election of Israel as a nation for God’s purposes.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the election of Israel as an act of sovereign grace that foreshadows the election of the church.

verses.text: For a period of about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.
verses.arminianNotes: God put up with them in the wilderness for forty years. Arminian commentators see God’s patience with a stubborn people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see God’s long-suffering faithfulness.

verses.text: When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land for an inheritance for about four hundred fifty years.
verses.arminianNotes: He destroyed seven nations and gave them the land. Arminian readers see God keeping his promise to Abraham.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s sovereignty over nations for the sake of his people.

verses.text: After these things, he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
verses.arminianNotes: He gave them judges until Samuel. Arminian expositors see God providing leaders time and again.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God preserving his people through every period.

verses.text: Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
verses.arminianNotes: They asked for a king, and God gave them Saul for forty years. Arminian readers see God granting a request that was not ideal.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s purposes advancing even through Israel’s mistaken desires.

verses.text: When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’
verses.arminianNotes: God raised up David, a man after his heart who would do all his will. Arminian commentators see David’s heart as the reason for his selection.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see God choosing and raising up David as he pleased.

verses.text: From this man’s offspring, God has brought salvation to Israel according to his promise,
verses.arminianNotes: From David’s offspring God has brought a Savior, Jesus. Arminian readers see the promise to David fulfilled.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the covenant line reaching its goal in Christ.

verses.text: before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: John preached a baptism of repentance to Israel before Jesus came. Arminian expositors see preparation through repentance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see John as the forerunner appointed by God.

verses.text: As John was fulfilling his course, he said, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’
verses.arminianNotes: John said he was not the one but was preparing the way. Arminian readers see humility in God’s messenger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see John pointing away from himself to Christ.

verses.text: “Brothers, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.
verses.arminianNotes: To descendants of Abraham and God-fearers, the message of salvation has been sent. Arminian commentators see salvation sent to all present.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the word of salvation sent by God.

verses.text: For those who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.
verses.arminianNotes: Jerusalem’s rulers did not recognize Jesus and fulfilled the prophets by condemning him. Arminian readers see ignorance that still led to guilt.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God fulfilling Scripture through the very rejection of Christ.

verses.text: Though they found no cause for death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.
verses.arminianNotes: Though they found no cause for death, they asked Pilate to execute him. Arminian expositors see injustice laid bare.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the innocent one condemned for the guilty.

verses.text: When they had fulfilled all things that were written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
verses.arminianNotes: When they fulfilled everything written about him, they buried him. Arminian readers see every prophecy accounted for.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the plan of God carried out to the last detail.

verses.text: But God raised him from the dead,
verses.arminianNotes: But God raised him from the dead. Arminian commentators see God’s answer to human rejection.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the turning point of history in a single sentence.

verses.text: and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.
verses.arminianNotes: He appeared for many days to his followers, who are now his witnesses. Arminian readers see reliable testimony.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see chosen witnesses carrying the message.

verses.text: We bring you good news of the promise made to the fathers,
verses.arminianNotes: We bring you the good news of the promise to the fathers. Arminian expositors see the gospel as fulfilled promise.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the unity of the covenant from Abraham to Christ.

verses.text: that God has fulfilled this to us, their children, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm, ‘You are my Son. Today I have become your father.’
verses.arminianNotes: God fulfilled it by raising Jesus, as Psalm 2 says: “You are my Son.” Arminian readers see the resurrection declaring Jesus’ identity.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the eternal Son publicly declared at his resurrection, as Romans 1:4 says.

verses.text: “Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’
verses.arminianNotes: He raised him, no more to return to decay, giving the holy and sure blessings of David. Arminian commentators see covenant promises secured.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the sure mercies of David guaranteed by the risen Christ.

verses.text: Therefore he says also in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.’
verses.arminianNotes: “You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.” Arminian readers see Psalm 16 applied again.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see apostolic agreement on the meaning of the psalm.

verses.text: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.
verses.arminianNotes: David served God’s purpose in his generation, died, and decayed. Arminian expositors see a faithful life within its time.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors note that David served “the counsel of God,” a phrase they see as describing God’s plan for each generation.

verses.text: But he whom God raised up saw no decay.
verses.arminianNotes: But the one God raised saw no decay. Arminian readers see the contrast that proves the point.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ alone fulfilling the promise.

verses.text: Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins;
verses.arminianNotes: Through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed. Arminian commentators see forgiveness announced to everyone present.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see forgiveness grounded in Christ’s person and work.

verses.text: and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: Everyone who believes is justified from all things the law of Moses could not justify. Arminian readers see justification by faith offered to anyone who believes.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see one of the clearest statements of justification by faith alone in Acts, anticipating Romans and Galatians.

verses.text: Beware therefore, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:
verses.arminianNotes: Beware lest what the prophets said come upon you. Arminian expositors see a warning that rejection is possible and serious.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the gospel offer accompanied by solemn warning.

verses.text: ‘Behold, you scoffers! Wonder and perish, for I work a work in your days, a work which you will in no way believe, if one declares it to you.’”
verses.arminianNotes: “Behold, you scoffers, wonder and perish.” Arminian readers see Habakkuk’s warning applied to those who refuse to believe.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s work proceeding even when people refuse to believe it.
